μὴ εἶναι πρὸς θάνατον τὴν ἀσθένειαν. οὐ τοσαύτης ἦν δόξης καὶ θαύματος τὸ ἐγεῖραι
τὸν Λάζαρον ἐκ τῆς νόσου, ὅσον τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν. 370 {3Jο 11, 6}3∆ιὰ
τοῦτο δὲ ἔμεινεν, ἵνα ἀποθάνῃ καὶ ταφῇ καὶ μὴ εἴπωσιν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὅτι καρωθέντα
αὐτὸν ἀνέστησεν. 371 {3Jο 11, 7}3∆ιὰ τοῦτο προλέγει, ἵνα μὴ ἀθρόον ἀπελθόντος

®

αὐτοῦ ἐκεῖ ταραχθῶσιν. 372 {3Jο 11, 8 9}3Τὸ δὲ ζητοῦσί σε λιθάσαι καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς ὡς
μήπω ὄντες ἀπηρτισμένοι καὶ νομίζοντες, ὅτι καὶ ἄκων ἔπασχεν, εἰπεῖν αὐτὸν τοῦτο
οὐχὶ δώδεκα ὧραί εἰσι καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. 373 {3Jο 11, 9}3Ὥσπερ ἄστατος ἡ ἡμέρα ἀπὸ ὥρας
εἰς ὥραν μεταβαίνουσα, οὕτω καὶ ἡ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γνώμη, ὅ ἐστιν τῶν Ἰουδαίων. εἰ
ὁ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ περιπατῶν οὐ προσκόπτει, πῶς ἐγὼ ὁ πάντας φωτίζων ὑπομένοιμι τὰ
τῶν ἀβουλήτων; 374 {3Jο 11, 15}3Ὡς πρὸς ζῶντα λέγει, ὅτι ἄγωμεν· αὐτῷ γὰρ ἔζη ὡς
θεῷ. 376 {3Jο 11, 16}3Ἵνα μὴ ἀφιλόστοργοι φανῶμεν, σπεύσωμεν ἐπὶ τὴν τοῦ φίλου
ἡμῶν σω τηρίαν ὑπερορῶντες τῶν Ἰουδαϊκῶν ἐπιβουλῶν. 377 {3Jο 11, 25}3Ζωὴν
ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν ὁ κύριος, οὐ ζῷον· τὸ μὲν γὰρ ζῷον δεκτικόν ἐστι ζωῆς, ἡ δὲ ζωὴ
παρεκτικὴ τοῦ ζῆν ὡς ἡ σοφία καὶ ὁ σοφός· ὁ μὲν λαμβάνει, ἡ δὲ δίδωσιν. 378 {3Jο
11, 31}3Εἰ μὴ οἰκονομίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦτο ἐγεγόνει, οὐκ ἂν ἐμέμνητο αὐτοῦ ὁ
εὐαγγελιστής· γέγονε δέ, ἵνα καὶ ἄκοντες παραγένωνται καὶ μαρτυρήσωσι τῷ
σημείῳ. 379 {3Jο 11, 33}3Λυπηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς καὶ ὁρῶν ἐν ἑαυτῷ κινηθεῖσαν τὴν
λύπην καὶ νεύουσαν τὴν σάρκα πρὸς δάκρυον ἐπιπλήττει τῇ σαρκὶ τῇ τοῦ ἁγίου
πνεύματος δυνάμει, ἥτις μὴ ἐνεγκοῦσα τὸ τῆς ἑνωθείσης αὐτῷ θεότητος κίνημα
τρέμει καὶ τῆς λύπης περικρατεῖ· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἥρμοζεν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ δακρύειν τῷ τὴν
ἐλπίδα τῆς ἀναστάσεως εἰσάγοντι. 380 {3Jο 11, 34}3Ὡς ἀφιλόκομπος τοῦτο εἶπεν καὶ
ἀγνοεῖν σχηματίζεται διὰ τὸ τῆς ἀνθρω πίνης φύσεως ταπεινὸν ὁ πάντα εἰδὼς ὡς
θεός, ἵνα πολλοὺς ἑλκύσῃ εἰς τὸν τόπον. 381 {3Jο 11, 34}3Οὐχ ὡς ἀγνοῶν ἐρωτᾷ ὁ
πρὸ πολλοῦ διαστήματος τοῦτο εἰδώς, ἀλλ' ἵνα προφάσει τοῦ ὑποδεῖξαι τὸν τόπον
ἔλθωσιν καὶ ἴδωσιν τὸ σημεῖον. 382 {3Jο 11, 35}3Συμπαθήσας τοῖς δακρύουσιν
ἐδάκρυσεν, οὐχ ὃν ἔμελλεν ἀνιστᾶν. 383 {3Jο 11, 38}3Πάλιν ἐπιτιμᾷ τῷ πάθει, ἵνα
μάθωμεν, ὅτι ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν ἀτρέπτως ὡς ἡμεῖς. 384 {3Jο 11, 39}3∆ιὰ τὴν
ὑπερβολὴν τοῦ θαύματος τρόπον τινὰ πάλιν ἀπιστεῖ ἡ Μάρθα. 385 {3Jο 11, 40}3Ἐν
τοῖς ὑπὲρ φύσιν φαίνεται ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ δόξα. διὰ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τῶν ἀκροατῶν τὴν τοῦ
πατρὸς δόξαν φησίν, διὰ τὸ ἀκενόδοξον οὐκ εἶπεν ὄψει τὴν δόξαν μου, ἀλλὰ τὴν τοῦ
πατρός. 386 {3Jο 11, 41}3Ἴσος δὲ ὢν τῷ πατρὶ εὐχαριστεῖ αὐτῷ, ἵνα ἡμεῖς τῷ ὑπὲρ
ἑαυτοὺς εὐχα ριστῶμεν. τοῦτο ἐπὶ φίλων λέγεται καὶ ὁμοτίμων. 387 {3Jο 11, 43}3Ὡς
πόρρωθεν οὖσαν τὴν ψυχὴν διὰ κραυγῆς καλεῖ, οὐ μὴν ὡς οὖσαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι, ὡς
Ἑλλήνων μυθεύουσι παῖδες. ἡ δὲ κραυγὴ τοῦ κυρίου τύπος ἦν τῆς «μεγάλης
σάλπιγγος» τῆς μελλούσης ἠχῆσαι ἐν τῇ κοινῇ ἀναστάσει. θεοπρεπὲς δὲ καὶ
βασιλικὸν τὸ κέλευσμα. 388 {3Jο 11, 44}3Οὕτω καὶ ἡ καθολικὴ μέλλει γενέσθαι
ἀνάστασις «ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ». ὅμοιον δὲ σημεῖον σχεδὸν τῆς
pass_a_gloss: the illness is not toward death. Raising from sickness was less glory than raising from the dead. He stayed so Lazarus would die and be buried and Jews could not claim a swoon. He foretells lest sudden departure trouble them. They cite stoning plots as if he suffers unwillingly, so he answers with the twelve hours saying. Day shifts hour by hour like Jewish opinion; if day walkers do not stumble, how would the one who enlightens all suffer the ill advised? Let us go speaks as to one living, for as God Lazarus lived to him. Thomas urges haste to the friend's salvation despite Jewish plots. He calls himself life, not a living being: living beings receive life, life supplies it, as wisdom gives and the wise receive. Jews coming with Mary happened by economy so even unwilling they witness the sign. Grieved, he rebukes flesh nodding to tears by the Spirit's power, which trembles under united Godhead and masters grief; the bringer of resurrection hope should not weep over the dead. He pretends not to know the tomb place from humility to draw many there, though as God he knew from afar. The question is pretext so they come and see, not ignorance. He weeps with weepers, not for the one he will raise. Again he rebukes the passion to show unchanged true humanity. Martha doubts again at the wonder's size. Beyond nature God's glory appears; for weak hearers and against vanity he names the Father's glory not his own. Equal to the Father he thanks him to teach us thanks toward the greater; such speech fits friends and equals. The cry calls a far soul, not a soul in the tomb as Greek myths say; it types the great trumpet of common resurrection and is a royal divine command. pass_b_english: the illness is not toward death. Raising Lazarus from sickness was not of such glory and wonder as raising him from the dead.
For this reason he stayed, that Lazarus might die and be buried and the Jews might not say he raised one who had only swooned.
For this reason he foretells, lest when he suddenly goes there they be troubled.

"They are seeking to stone you" and what follows they said as not yet perfected and thinking that he also suffered unwillingly, so that he said this: "Are there not twelve hours" and what follows (John 11:9).

Just as the day is unstable, shifting from hour to hour, so also is human opinion—that is, the Jews'. If the one who walks in day does not stumble, how would I who enlighten all undergo the things of the ill-advised?
He speaks as to one living when he says "let us go"; for to him Lazarus lived as God.
Lest we appear without affection, let us hasten to our friend's salvation, overlooking Jewish plots.
The Lord called himself life, not a living being; for a living being is receptive of life, but life is what supplies living, as wisdom and the wise: the one receives, the other gives.
If this had not happened by God's economy, the evangelist would not have mentioned it; it happened so that even unwilling they might come and witness the sign.

Christ, grieved and seeing grief moved in himself and the flesh nodding toward tears, rebukes the flesh by the Holy Spirit's power, which, not bearing the movement of the Godhead united to it, trembles and masters the grief; for it was not fitting for the one who brings the hope of resurrection to weep over a dead man.
As one without love of display he said this and pretends not to know, because of the lowliness of human nature—he who knows all as God—that he might draw many to the place.
He asks not as ignorant, he who knew this from a long distance, but so that on the pretext of pointing out the place they may come and see the sign.
Sympathizing with those who wept, he wept—not for the one he was about to raise.
Again he rebukes the passion, that we may learn that he became man without change as we are.
Because of the excess of the wonder Martha somehow again disbelieves.
In things beyond nature God's glory appears. Because of the hearers' weakness he says the Father's glory; because of freedom from vanity he did not say "you will see my glory" but the Father's.
Being equal to the Father he thanks him, that we may give thanks to the one above ourselves. This is said among friends and equals.

As if the soul were far off he calls with a cry, not as if it were in the tomb, as the Greeks' children mythologize. The Lord's cry was a type of the "great trumpet" that will sound in the common resurrection. The command is God-befitting and royal.
